newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL stocks seen in mixed pattern.
newsitem.headline: KL stocks seen in mixed pattern.

text.p: Kuala Lumpur stocks could stay in a mixed pattern, with blue chips expected to resume an uptrend but secondary shares facing further correction, dealers said.
"I'm looking at downside support of 580 (on the Second Board)," said William Chan, an institutional dealer with Seagroatt and Campbell. "It now looks very, very vulnerable."
On Wednesday, the Composite Index ended down 0.56 points to 1,234.17, while the Second Board index sank 22.54 points to 594.22.
"We expect volatility on the main board and Second Board," Audrey Ho, research director of Mohaiyani Securities. "The consolidation for the Second Board is still not over yet."

Finance and banking shares could continue to draw interest, amid speculation about further banking mergers, dealers said. Earlier this week, stockbroker Rashid Hussain concluded a 2.16 billion ringgit deal to buy Kwong Yik bank from Maybank.
Wall Street ended down 29.07 points overnight in quiet pre-Thanksgiving day trading. The market will be closed on Thursday for the holiday.
